name: STRAFPERLAGGEN
description: Strafperlaggen is a variant of Perlaggen, a traditional Tyrolean card game, typically played by 3 players. It uses a 33-card German-suited deck (Weli is the 33rd card). Similar to Perlaggen, players aim to win 'figures' (Gleich, Hanger, Spiel). The 'Straf' (Penalty) aspect likely refers to stricter rules or penalty points for failures.

content.text: Strafperlaggen is a variant of Perlaggen, a traditional Tyrolean card game, typically played by 3 players. It uses a 33-card German-suited deck (Weli is the 33rd card). Similar to Perlaggen, players aim to win 'figures' (Gleich, Hanger, Spiel). The 'Straf' (Penalty) aspect likely refers to stricter rules or penalty points for failures.

Perlaggen appeared in the Tyrol in the early 19th century; the first comprehensive rules were published in 1853 (Das Tiroler National- oder Perlagg-Spiel) and the game was recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2016. Strafperlaggen is a three-player variant played in and around Hall and Absam, east of Innsbruck, which adds penalty points (Strafpunkte) for betting or holding a figure and failing to win it.
Three players only; each plays for themselves.
33-card German-suited pack (32 cards plus Weli, the Six of Bells).
Seven cards each: deal 3 each, turn trump (if acorn turn until non-acorn), then 4 each. Dealer may exchange natural trump for turned Perlagg or acorns for acorn Perlaggen.
